title: Cool Yoghurt Rice with Mustard Seeds, Curry Leaves and Pomegranate
summary: Soft, lightly mashed rice folded with yoghurt, milk and ginger until creamy, then topped with a crisp tempering of cashews, mustard seeds, curry leaves and chillies. Jewel-like pomegranate seeds and coriander add freshness and crunch.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
plain whole-milk yoghurt, at room temperature
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Cook the rice soft
steps.text: Rinse the rice until the water runs almost clear, then put it in the saucepan with the 600 ml water and 0.5 tsp salt. Bring to a boil, cover and simmer on low for 20 minutes until very soft. Take off the heat and mash lightly with a spoon so some grains break. The extra water and light mashing release starch, which gives the finished dish its creamy, pudding-like texture.

steps.title: Cool until just warm
steps.text: Spread the rice out in the shallow bowl or on the tray and leave for about 20-30 minutes, no longer than 1 hour, until it is just warm to the touch. Spreading it thinly lets the heat escape quickly and safely. This matters because yoghurt stirred into hot rice splits and turns sour.

steps.title: Mix with yoghurt
steps.text: In the large bowl, stir the rice with the yoghurt, milk, ginger and 0.25 tsp salt until it is creamy, like a thick rice pudding. Add a little more milk if it seems stiff. Room-temperature yoghurt blends more smoothly with warm rice than cold yoghurt straight from the fridge.

steps.title: Fry the tempering
steps.text: Heat the oil in the small pan over medium heat and fry the cashews for 2-3 minutes, stirring, until lightly golden. Add the mustard seeds, and once they pop add the cumin, asafoetida if using, curry leaves, green chilli and dried chillies, frying for 10-20 seconds until fragrant. Pour the sizzling oil and spices over the rice. Hot oil carries the flavour of the spices through the whole dish.

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.text: Scatter over the pomegranate seeds and coriander and serve at room temperature or lightly chilled. The sweet-tart pomegranate brightens the mild yoghurt and adds a juicy crunch against the soft rice.

tips: A common mistake is adding yoghurt to hot rice, which makes it split and sour; cool the rice until just warm first, within 1 hour.
Note on asafoetida: most ground asafoetida is blended with wheat flour, so choose a gluten-free brand or leave it out if you need the dish gluten-free.
The rice firms up as it stands, so loosen it with a spoonful of milk before serving.
Keep a close eye on the cashews, as they go from golden to burnt very quickly.
storage: Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour and eat cold within 24 hours, loosened with a spoonful of milk. Do not reheat. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
